Technical & price structure: In plain terms: the marked assets net of debt and minority are ~EGP 8–9 a share. Everything above depends on land being monetised at the marks and the holdco/minority discount narrowing. That's the bet.
Monte Carlo — where could the price go?: Below EGP 5.92 — the bear-case value, which assumes the land is never monetised at the marks and the holdco discount never narrows — the market would be pricing in worse than our most pessimistic case, the point where we’d rebuild the study.

One Monte Carlo model, 50,000 paths, driven by 10 outside forces: the central-bank rate, the EGP/USD rate, inflation, foreign money flows, oil, regional politics, the structural NAV discount, land monetisation and sales velocity, mortgage lending, and EGP step-devaluation risk. Full mechanics in the methodology .
